newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. Robotics unveils new 56 kilobit modem.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics unveils new 56 kilobit modem.

text.p: Modem manufacturer U.S. Robotics said Wednesday it has developed a new computer modem that can operate at 56 kilobits per second -- a new high in transmission speed -- and is comparable to high-speed ISDN networks.

U.S. Robotics, in a statement issued by its German public relations representative, said the x2 modem will begin field testing in November and will be available to customers beginning in the first quarter of 1997.
U.S. Robotics said Tuesday it would introduce a new technology Wednesday, and analysts had believed it might be the long-awaited faster modem.

The fastest dial-up modem currently on the market is 33.6 kilobits per second. Computer users surfing the World Wide Web portion of the Internet can see Web pages more quickly and download more swiftly using an ISDN -- Integrated Services Digital Network -- connection, which enables copper phone wires to handle heavier traffic than that for which they were originally designed.

The Skokie, Ill.-based company said it has signed up 32 on-line service providers to field test and market the modems. They include America Online, the No. 1 online service in the world, and IBM Global Network.
Customers who buy existing Sportster modems from U.S. Robotics will need simple and relatively inexpensive upgrades, the company said.
The upgrade will be available in January.
U.S. Robotics' stock, which has climbed recently in anticipation of the announcement, slipped 37.5 cents to $77.625 on Nasdaq in late morning trading.
